title: Two Kinds of Sound
logline: At a wind-scoured fish landing site, auctioneers' calls compete with gusts and surf, and buyers lean in close to tell a voice from the weather.
human_question: When the wind and a human voice make the same kind of sound, how does anyone tell them apart?

premise.story: A morning's fish auction on an exposed beach, told through the auctioneers, buyers and crews whose livelihoods depend on being heard, or on hearing correctly.
premise.place: A coastal fish landing site where boats arrive, catches are auctioned on the sand, and the wind is a constant.
premise.experience: Shouted bids and hand signs, gusts and surf swallowing words, buyers straining forward to catch a number, a catch changing hands.

concept_links.why: The source draws exactly this distinction: speech is mind-born sound, and wind noise is temperature-born sound. The same kind of sense object, sound, arises here from two different origins at once, audible side by side.
Sound is described as dying where it arises, so what reaches a buyer's ear across a windy beach is only sound's own moving trace, which is why a call can be lost entirely in a gust.

what_camera_could_observe: Boats landing and catches carried up the beach
Shouted bids, hand signs and gestures
Gusts and surf briefly drowning out calls
Buyers leaning in, cupping ears, asking for a number to be repeated
The catch changing hands and the crowd moving to the next lot
what_must_be_real: Real prices, real catches and real trade. No staged auction or repeated takes; the fishers' and buyers' actual stakes must lead.

possible_arc.opening: Boats landing at first light, the crowd gathering.
possible_arc.turn: The wind rising against the calling, a bid nearly lost.
possible_arc.ending_open: The last lot sold, or the morning's trade ending as it actually does.

requirements: An active fish auction on an open, windy beach or landing site
Fishers, auctioneers and buyers willing to be filmed at their real work
Enough wind on the day to make the sound contrast real, not staged

suggestions.name: Fish landing sites on the eastern coast
suggestions.why: The east coast has open, often windy beach landing sites with beach-based auctions.
suggestions.season_notes: Wind conditions vary by monsoon season; needs local confirmation.
suggestions.verify: A specific landing site, its auction practice and willingness to be filmed are unverified.

risks: Could stay a sound-design exercise with no real human stake
Must follow real buyers and sellers and their actual livelihoods, not just the weather
drop_if: No auction with real wind and sound contrast on the filming days
No consent from traders and fishers

connections.note: Two senses under pressure at once: sound lost to wind, colour lost to shifting light.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
